title: Kernel profiling, warmstart orchestration, and granular KV reuse policy
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: For long-form and multiturn workloads we observe tail latency spikes and increased token cost due to fragmented KV residency and suboptimal kernel choice when requests transition across sequence lengths and model variants. Existing heuristics either overreserve KV segments (wasting memory) or are too reactive (causing decode stalls).

Goal: Implement a combined system of (1) per-host kernel profiling + runtime vetting so the scheduler picks the best kernel variant for a given kernel shape and hardware topology, (2) a lightweight warmstart orchestration that issues targeted KV warmups (warmstart) for high-probability token spans to reduce decode stalls, and (3) a granular KV reuse policy that increases reuse across similar sequences while bounding cross-tenant spill and fragmentation. The system should improve 99th percentile decode latency by >=15% and reduce wasted KV memory by >=10% for our benchmark suites.

Scope and components: 
- Kernel profiler: offline microbenchmarks produce a kernel-scorecard per model variant + hardware (A100/H100/GPU gen). A small runtime self-check validates that the chosen kernel meets latency/cost predictions for the active tensor shapes.
- Warmstart orchestrator: a per-shard controller that converts inference traffic signals (initial prefix tokens, beam branching, rerank calls) into targeted KV warmstart operations. Warmstarts are small, cheap prefills that prime the decoder’s KV slots for the next 16-64 tokens expected. Warmstarts are throttled by a lease admission controller to preserve memory SLOs.
- Granular KV reuse policy: Replace the current LRU-only eviction with a two-axis policy: (a) affinity buckets based on recent decode shape and prompt-hash, (b) a decay-weighted reuse score that favors fragments that historically led to cache hits. Eviction promotes low-reuse fragments while allowing safe cross-sequence reuse when tenant isolation budgets permit.

Key constraints and trade-offs: 
- Memory vs latency: Warmstarts improve latency but consume transient KV residency. Admission uses token-cost budgeting per shard to avoid eviction storms.
- Fairness: Affinity buckets can bias toward high-volume tenants; enforce tenant weights and per-tenant soft quotas.
- Complexity: Kernel vetting adds startup overhead; mitigate by caching vetting results and running checks in background for warm hosts.

Metrics to track: 99/95/50 pct decode latency, per-token GPU time, KV occupancy and fragmentation ratio, warmstart hit rate, eviction churn, customer-impacting request failures.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged canary -> per-region 5% -> 25% -> global. Monitor SLO dashboards and automated rollback triggers (latency regression >5% on P95 or eviction churn >2x).

Deliverables: design doc + simulator, kernel scorecard pipeline, warmstart admission service, KV reuse policy implementation, e2e benchmarks, canary runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Offline kernel scorecards exist for top 6 models and are consumed by the runtime
Warmstart orchestrator issues targeted warmstart operations without exceeding 10% additional average KV occupancy per shard
Granular KV reuse policy reduces fragmentation ratio by >=10% on long-form benchmarks
No customer-facing error rate increase; P95 decode latency improved by >=15% on internal pageset
Feature is behind an opt-in flag with safe rollback and automated monitoring alerts
comments: 2026-02-16 | Aisha Malik: Initial spike analysis attached. Observed 2.3x increase in decode tail when model crossing boundary from seq_len 1024->2048. Proposing warmstart instead of global overreservation.
2026-02-20 | Ronan Kline: POC kernel profiler runs completed on A100/H100. H100 favors kernel variant v3 for seq<512; A100 prefers v2. Workload variance noted for quant-8 models.
2026-02-24 | Priya Sharma (PM): Please include tenant-weight testing — we saw a customer report where reuse heuristics caused increased cold starts for small tenants. Add per-tenant quotas to plan.

2026-03-01 | Marco Ortega (Eng reviewer): Reviewed warmstart admission design. Concern: warmstart storms during bursty traffic. Recommend adding backpressure token_bucket and a grace window after eviction events.
2026-03-05 | Design review (Emily Zhao): UX for runtime tuning removed; we'll expose only high-level knobs (aggression and memory cap). Detailed metrics remain internal.
2026-03-08 | Ronan Kline: Integration test results — warmstart hit rate 42% on long-doc dataset, eviction churn down 18%. Need more stress tests under multi-tenant interference.
